newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks close bourse down as dollar weakens.
newsitem.headline: German stocks close bourse down as dollar weakens.

text.p: German shares closed floor trade weaker on Tuesday after the dollar weakened against the mark and as Wall Street losses and comments by German economic institutes held the market back.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares reversed gains made on Monday when it had reached above the crucial 2,700 point mark, to end down 30.21 points, or 1.12 percent, at 2,673.62.

Forecasts from the country's six leading economic research institutes predicted the German public sector deficit would amount to 3.5 percent of economic output in 1997, well above the Maastricht Treaty's three percent goal.

The bi-annual forecast also said German interest rates may need to rise if money supply growth remained above target levels, a conclusion that immediately sent the German mark rising against the dollar, in turn putting pressure on export-oriented German stocks.
Chemical company BASF AG fell, but less than the market trend, ending off eight pfennigs at 48.80 marks, with dealers saying a large buy order was supporting the stock.

The biggest loser of the DAX companies, was German retailer Metro, which ended down three percent, or 3.90 marks, at 126.50 marks. Dealers said the stock's late recovery on Monday after the day's early fall had been overdone.
The stock had fallen after German prosecutors said they had opened an investigation into the firm's plans to off-set losses from a recent merger with other store groups.
Competing retailer Karstadt, in contrast, was stronger than the market trend, ending down just two marks, or 0.36 percent, at 550 marks.
Dealers said all eyes would be trained on the U.S. for the rest of the week as a stream of data is released.
